On all the implementations of Mixpanel I've been involved in, I've made it a point to not send any PII to Mixpanel. It's not needed for Mixpanel analytics to work, Mixpanel is not a CRM.

Mixpanel's post is very poorly written. This is basically a textbook example of how not to handle this situation. The OpenAI disclosure is a better summary of what happened than Mixpanel is stating directly.
OpenAI: 'After reviewing this incident, OpenAI has terminated its use of Mixpanel' - a pretty damning statement about a vendor you don't see written often publicly like that.
Mixpanel has 'session replay' support and it's easy to let things like names and emails slip through, given docs show identify-users guide sending emails as identifiers.
As an engineer who has used Mixpanel at multiple companies it has always annoyed me that what you get for what you pay seems quite poor.

Mixpanel has the most obscure pricing model of any SAAS I've ever tried to integrate with... When we 'upgraded' from their free tier to a paid tier we were DOWNGRADED from 20M events a month to 10K events a month.

To match what they provide in their free tier (20M events), the paid cost is $2,289 USD/month. So basically we can either pay $2,289/month, or pay nothing, and still get the same number of tracked events. Bizarre... we've moved on.
The group-level / account-level stuff is pretty big for B2B SaaS companies to be able to consider using it. And it's tucked away on one of Mixpanel's higher price plans.

Previously used Mixpanel (under free startup package), but dropped it after that expired because it was going to be $x,000 per month... we'd never spent enough time setting it up and weren't getting a huge amount of value from it.
The whole point of something like Mixpanel is to make analytics accessible to non-engineers... If there's one reason Mixpanel is still in business, that's because of this.
